title: packaging/docker/run.sh must stay POSIX sh (no bash)
answers: Why can't I use bash syntax in the Docker entrypoint script?
How do I get an env var by dynamic name in run.sh?
Script breaks in the alpine docker image with 'bad substitution' or '[[: not found'
Can I add bashisms to packaging/docker/run.sh?
body:
Symptom: entrypoint fails in the alpine container with errors like 'bad substitution', '[[: not found', or similar shell errors.
Root cause: the alpine Docker image no longer installs bash (Dockerfile apk add lines dropped 'bash') to shrink attack surface/image size, so run.sh runs under ash/dash, not bash.
Fix pattern: avoid bashisms in packaging/docker/run.sh — no indirect variable expansion `${!var}` (use `printenv "$var_name"` or `eval var="\$$var_name"`), no `[[ ]]` tests (use `case`/`[ ]`), no `$(< file)` (use `$(cat file)`).
Constraints: applies to packaging/docker/run.sh and any other script baked into the production Docker image (shebang `#!/bin/sh`); does not apply to build-time scripts run in stages that still install bash (Dockerfile build-stage apk add).
applies: packaging/docker/run.sh and scripts executed inside the final alpine Docker image

search: The script packaging/docker/run.sh must use only POSIX sh syntax because the Alpine Docker image no longer installs bash, so scripts run under ash/dash and bashisms cause entrypoint failures ('bad substitution', '[[: not found'). Avoid indirect variable expansion ${!var} (use printenv "$var_name" or eval), [[ ]] conditionals (use case or [ ]), and $(< file) (use $(cat file)). This applies to any script with shebang #!/bin/sh baked into the final production image, but not to build-stage scripts run in Dockerfile stages that still install bash. Check packaging/docker/run.sh and the Dockerfile for compliance.
